reviewer.identity: Independent Codex GPT-6 agent; exact variant and reasoning setting not exposed
reviewer.fresh_input: Neutral brief, frozen manifest, actual reader sources and primary texts. No previous Opus verdicts, writer ledgers, repair scripts, current-state files or history read.

audience: Undergraduate calculus, basic linear algebra, expectation, variance, SD and density known. Neural and specialized stochastic/information meanings must be taught.

scope.sidecars: All six YAML files, including captions and alt text read. Mathematical caption content checked; artwork pixels not accepted.
scope.upstream: Memory meanings and baseline in 00-reading-guide.md/.yaml; Part I introduction/map in chapter-plan.yaml; relevant glossary entries. Non-memory orientation facts belong to their assigned groups.

judgment_format: Each entry is a retain judgment. Locations are current source line numbers. Shared source BF means Burak and Fiete main paper and supporting text. Primary evidence files and actual hashes appear below.

judgments.claim: Repeated motor spikes sustain tension; elasticity, viscosity and inertia play different roles.
judgments.reason: Anatomical muscle and cranial nerve roles match Dragoi 8.2A-B. Viscosity and inertia give no steady holding torque. Nonlinear real mechanics are not ruled out.
judgments.evidence: Dragoi 8.2A-B; Anderson 2009 Introduction; Major 2004 Fig.1.

judgments.claim: Outgoing spike traces decay; weights set input; the transfer function sets firing rate.
judgments.reason: A unit delta pulse raises dimensionless s_i by one. Count and exponential-convolution forms agree. W_ij maps j to i; model input is not claimed to be membrane voltage.
judgments.evidence: BF main p.5 Eqs.7-9; SI I.

judgments.claim: Tuning patterns represent values; estimated rate maps differ from expected functions.
judgments.reason: Slopes carry rate per degree units; neuron index is distinguished from physical location. Positive-rate range and CA3/CA1 versus memory-mechanism limits remain explicit.
judgments.evidence: BF main pp.1-2; Mainali model; Maimon 2026 primary online Introduction/Discussion extracts.

judgments.claim: Poisson counts have equal mean and variance; recurrent noise independence is local and conditional.
judgments.reason: Independent-bin limit and factorial moments are correct. exp(-1)=0.367879; pooled relative SD=1/sqrt(20)=0.223607. Whole recurrent trains are not claimed independent or Poisson-counted. CV and Fano factor are distinguished.
judgments.evidence: BF Eqs.7-11; SI I and S43; count algebra recomputed.

judgments.claim: Ring and two-unit simulations test the model prediction rather than animal performance.
judgments.reason: 1024 units, Euler step, conditional Bernoulli draw, h=0.1ms, tau=10ms, maximum-rate angle and wrapped displacement match Methods. Aggregate population counts are separated from the ring one-spike rule. MSD/log slopes and units are correct.
judgments.evidence: BF main p.6 Network Simulations; Fig.2 caption; p.5 experimental limits.

judgments.claim: Shared drive, private noise, bias, gain, muscle response and measurement error affect different statistics.
judgments.reason: Covariance and MSD identities are correct with the stated independence. Gain multiplies its own variance contribution by its square. Independent position errors add twice their variance. Correlation with one cell does not assign all motion to that cell.
judgments.evidence: Displayed covariance/MSD identities checked directly; Ben-Shushan Methods Eqs.2-7 supplies the connected setting; full eye-paper check belongs to that group.

judgments.claim: Active torque balances elastic pull; integration maintains the command; plasticity adjusts it.
judgments.reason: Equilibrium and B/K relaxation follow from the torque equation. The one-spring approximation is labeled. Cannon original Summary explicitly reports reversible effects and >20s versus 200ms. Major reports training and reversal without identifying a cellular learning rule.
judgments.evidence: Anderson 2009; Cannon and Robinson 1987 original Summary 2-3; Major 2004.

judgments.claim: Stable directions recover while a changed memory coordinate can remain.
judgments.reason: dot x=-a x and dot theta=0 follow directly. From (50,30), common (+3,+3) returns at 5 degrees; (+3,-3) stays at 6.5 degrees. Mutual inhibition has common-mode decay 2/tau in its linear interior.
judgments.evidence: BF Introduction, Fig.1 and p.6 mutual inhibition; example algebra checked.

judgments.claim: Independent unbiased retained steps give variance 2Dt; drift and boundaries require separate treatment.
judgments.reason: Variance sum and Brownian covariance min(s,t) are correct. D=.02 gives RMS .118322 degrees at .35s; crossover with v=.1 occurs at 4s with .16 square degrees per contribution. Equal per-axis D is required for 2dDt. RMS is not a path boundary.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S30-S32; Brownian, bias and numeric calculations checked directly.

judgments.claim: A fixed random map differs from a represented value wandering over time.
judgments.reason: Revisits evaluate the same expected function while spikes can vary. Neither spatial irregularity nor diffusion alone determines the other. No joint circuit test is claimed.
judgments.evidence: Mainali model/STAR Methods; BF model setting.

judgments.claim: The return endpoint assigns memory; Gaussian noise approximates weak aggregate input fluctuations.
judgments.reason: State s and coordinate theta are distinct. Conditional compensator and Gaussian increments match leading covariance; sqrt(r)dB is dimensionless. Replication gives 1/n variance at fixed mean. Leading weak-noise status and finite-network limits are explicit.
judgments.evidence: BF main p.2 coordinate definition; SI S1-S10.

judgments.claim: The left zero vector extracts the surviving displacement, which need not be perpendicular projection.
judgments.reason: Taylor expansion gives K; differentiating F(sbar)=0 gives Ku=0. v^TK=0 and v^Tu=1 discard stable modes and normalize the coordinate. Tilted decay gives x_infinity=x0+(a/lambda)y0. Symmetric W need not give symmetric K.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S7-S18; tilted example solved directly.

judgments.claim: Projected spike variance gives 2D=sum v_i^2 r_i and its tensor form.
judgments.reason: Left multiplication removes return flow and independence removes cell cross terms. One cell can move several coordinates, so tensor cross terms can remain. Local/leading-order conditions are retained.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S14-S15,S21-S27.

judgments.claim: Symmetric W gives v proportional to input slope and the squared numerator.
judgments.reason: Chain rule and v normalization give the displayed expression, independently confirmed by the 2017 correction. Inhibition gives s=(b+/-theta)/2 and D=b/(2tau). Coordinate conversion to the earlier rate/angle example is correct and boundaries are excluded.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S16-S18; main p.6; official correction DOI 10.1073/pnas.1706051114.

judgments.claim: Zero-drift Ito diffusion gives density evolution, wrapping, and state-dependent variance.
judgments.reason: Generator expansion and integrations by parts are correct. Uniform wrapped MSE is pi^2/3. The t^2 coefficient is D Ddoubleprime. Mutual excitation gives D=theta/(4tau), consistent with projected variance theta*t/(2tau) and S41; the S40 factor discrepancy is correctly labeled an independent check.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S28-S41.

judgments.claim: Variance does not determine systematic drift; correlated elementary noise changes projection.
judgments.reason: Conversion gives bbprime/2=Dprime/2 and is used as a possible scale, not an exact neural drift. Orders dt/N and sqrt(dt/N) are correct. General covariance gives v^TQv; no theorem for all correlated models is claimed.
judgments.evidence: BF SI Systematic drift pp.4-5,S19-S20; main p.5 Discussion.

judgments.claim: The figures distinguish retained memory motion, decoding uncertainty and simulation tests.
judgments.reason: Written descriptions match original captions: return-flow coordinate, finite-sample uncertainty, ring/inhibition comparisons, sigmoidal lower bound and wrapped error saturation. This judges textual meaning, not artwork pixels.
judgments.evidence: BF Figs.1-2 captions and p.6 Methods.

judgments.claim: Poisson Fisher information is local probability sensitivity; inverse information bounds locally unbiased variance.
judgments.reason: Background example quarters information at fixed slope. Likelihood, score variance, hJ units and Cramer Rao proof are correct. Positive rates, nearby unbiasedness, regularity, priors, distant ambiguity and nonattainment by arbitrary decoders are qualified.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S42-S44; main Eq.3; displayed score and Cauchy Schwarz derivations checked.

judgments.claim: The physical heuristic is distinct from proof; exponential transfer is sufficient but not generally necessary.
judgments.reason: v.u=1 gives 2DJ>=tau^-2. Equality is v_i=c*rprime_i/r_i. Excitation with b0=0 has stable difference mode and attains equality for every positive theta with a linear rule. Inhibition gives J=.05,D=1000 at zero and J=1/15,bound=750 at theta=100. Counterexamples support the narrower equality claim.
judgments.evidence: BF main Eq.4 and p.3 heuristic; SI S45-S51; example calculations checked directly.

judgments.claim: The matrix bound controls all coordinate combinations when J is invertible.
judgments.reason: U^TV=I, U^TU=tau^2J, V^TV=2D have correct shapes. Expanding the residual Q gives Q^TQ=2D-tau^-2J^-1. Singular J is not silently inverted.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S52-S56; residual expansion checked.

judgments.claim: N, rate, time-constant and width comparisons depend on the quantities held fixed.
judgments.reason: Replication gives D~1/N,J~N. Rate and tau scaling preserve stated retuning conditions. Width integral gives rho*a*w^(d-2); isotropy precedes the diagonal inverse. Fixed total firing gives J~w^-2 in every dimension. Sensory/internal compatibility remains conditional on matching tuning curves.
judgments.evidence: BF pp.2,4-6 and sensory-tuning footnote; displayed controlled scalings checked.

judgments.claim: Storage and cue-state readout variances add under stated model assumptions.
judgments.reason: Independent Gaussian process/observation errors are explicitly introduced; same-spike dependence is explicitly excluded. Conditional zero readout mean makes E[se]=0. Translation invariance fixes its variance. Priors, boundaries and state dependence need changes.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S57-S63; covariance argument checked.

judgments.claim: Equal weighting gives 2DL/3+1/(JL) and a finite best duration.
judgments.reason: The Brownian double integral is L^3/3; minimization gives sqrt(3/(2DJ)) and (2/sqrt3)*sqrt(2D/J). Constant coefficients are only a local application to the two-cell network.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S76-S81; integral/minimization checked.

judgments.claim: Backward Gaussian precision gives coth variance and a saturation scale rather than a hard cutoff.
judgments.reason: Transition convolution adds 2Dh and observation adds Jh precision, giving Pprime=J-2DP^2. Its solution and short-L expansion match the displayed variance. coth at 1,2,3 equals 1.313035,1.037315,1.004970; naive SD ratio=1.074570. No implemented neural readout circuit is claimed.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S58-S75, with S71 sign independently resolved by recursion.

judgments.claim: Independent spike thinning reduces J to alpha*J without changing full-network D.
judgments.reason: Rates/slopes both scale by alpha, so time and limiting variance scale by alpha^-1/2. A neuron fraction is not automatically an information fraction. Full and partial access numbers and storage-error sums agree.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S82 and Fig.S2; displayed arithmetic checked.

judgments.claim: The stated two-stage model uses tau+tau_m; additive Gaussian noise changes equality conditions.
judgments.reason: Negative rate-decay block matches S84. Left b=tau_m*a and normalization give the sum of times with noise only in s. Matched q/h observation noise and q*sum(v^2) diffusion give the same bound; linear transfer is sufficient for equal q.
judgments.evidence: BF SI S84-S95; matrix/noise calculations checked.

judgments.claim: Normalized readout curves differ; main Eq.6 is not a universal consequence of the other formulas.
judgments.reason: Curves normalize to coth(z) and z/3+1/z, with naive optimum sqrt3. From 2DJ>=tau^-2 follows sqrt(2D/J)<=2Dtau, so it cannot supply the printed lower bound. The strict example gives .0205 versus .021. This is restricted to the local independent Gaussian model and not called an author correction. Diffusion is not a leak.
judgments.evidence: BF main Eqs.4-6/Fig.3; SI S57,S75,S83 and p.17 Integration time constant.

conclusion: No required truth/reasoning correction established in the inspected connected text. Keep the reviewed explanations and qualifications. Stage 1 only; wording, flow, whole-book and release acceptance are not granted.
